newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil BNDES appeals latest CVRD injunction.
newsitem.headline: Brazil BNDES appeals latest CVRD injunction.

text.p: Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) has appealed against an injunction which halted the bidding for mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), a judicial spokeswoman said.

The spokeswoman for the Regional Federal Tribunal (TRF) in Rio de Janeiro said the court's president would consider the petition against the court order, which dramatically interrupted the auction in the Rio bourse just after midday.
She added that another injunction had been granted by a lower court in Rio de Janeiro and that BNDES lawyers had still to lodge a petition against that one.

In the southern state of Rio Grande do Sul, court officials confirmed that an injunction still outstanding Tuesday morning had since been revoked. BNDES officials earlier said that court order had been overturned, allowing the auction to begin.
The sale of up to 45 percent of CVRD's voting shares had been on hold since April 29 because of a flurry of court injunctions.
On Monday night the government won what was regarded as a crucial legal victory when a high court judge in Brasilia overruled a host of those legal barriers to the auction.
But the high court ruling did not give the government blanket protection from furtther law suits.
According to BNDES officials, the ruling only applied to so-called "popular actions", which can be filed by any Brazilian citizen registered to vote.
It did not apply to so-called "public civil actions", which are restricted to associations and organizations with an interest in the issue being contested.
The injunction that halted the bidding midway Tuesday came from a public civil action brought by employees of CVRD.

The privatization of the world's largest iron ore exporter has sparked considerable opposition, with critics ranging from former presidents to the church accusing the government of selling off the country's wealth for next to nothing.
If the government manages to overturn the two remaining injunctions in Rio de Janeiro, it intends to resume the auction on Tuesday, officials said.
